commits.message:
feat(color): ramp — a number becomes a colour over ordered stops, in OKLCH (#92)

* feat(color): ramp — a number becomes a colour over ordered stops, in OKLCH

`ColorRamp` (src/themes/ramp.ts) maps a measurement onto ordered colour
stops: `linear` interpolates between adjacent stops in OKLCH, `step` holds
each stop until the next — a threshold cascade (`≥ 50 warning, ≥ 80 error`)
written as data. One class, the easing a value. Values clamp at both ends
and a value on a stop returns that stop's colour byte for byte, so a step
ramp never paints a colour the author did not write.

`Oklch.mix` is the interpolation: shorter hue arc, and an achromatic
endpoint adopts the other's hue (CSS Color 4's powerless rule), using the
same ACHROMATIC_EPS `fromRgba` pins hue by.

The template binding `ramp <value> <easing> <position> <color> …` sits
beside `color` in `paletteFuncs`: stops are colour references resolved
through `resolveColorRef` against the live palette on every evaluation, so
a ramp over palette names recolours with the theme. The argument list is
one float/string cycle end to end, typed by the engine's `alternating`
gate; the pairing and the references are parsed once in `colorStops`.

Docs, both colour demos, and tests cover the module, the OKLCH mix, and
the binding.

* docs(ramp): the ramp example builds an engine that has ramp; stale reader lists stop naming readers

The template-bindings doc's ramp example used createRichTextEngine(), which
wires richTextFuncs() alone — ramp is a palette function (its stops may be
palette names) and lives in paletteFuncs, so the pasted snippet threw at
evaluation. It now builds the engine the way the doc's own palette section
does, with both maps.

The ACHROMATIC_EPS comment enumerated its readers and went stale the moment
mix() became a third; it now states the invariant without a list, so no
reader can stale it again. The studio's ramp import label pointed at
section 6; the demo lives in section 5.

* fix(oklch): one achromatic rule for every Oklch producer; mix refuses t outside [0, 1]; ramp names a missing value

`mix` pinned no hue on its result, so `gray.mix(blue, 0)` was a zero-chroma
colour wearing blue's hue — a gray `fromRgba` would never produce, breaking
"achromatic means h = 0". The pin is now ONE function, `hueOf(c, h)` beside
`ACHROMATIC_EPS`, applied by `fromRgba`, `applyKey` and `mix` to their
results (the two inline pins are gone); the constructor still passes
intermediates through by contract. The lerp moves to the endpoint-exact
`a*(1-t) + b*t` form, so t = 1 lands on `toward` bit-for-bit on every axis.

`mix` is interpolation, not extrapolation: t outside [0, 1] (NaN included)
is a RangeError. `ColorRamp.at` already returns stop colours before mix
sees an out-of-range t.

`{{ ramp }}` with no arguments reached the body and threw the misleading
"needs an easing after the value"; one arity check over the whole argument
list now names what is missing and how many arrived.

The two module comments name `color` AND `ramp` as the palette-dependent
functions.

* docs(template-bindings): richTextFuncs' docstring names both theme-bound functions, color and ramp

* test(template-bindings): the palette-bound inventory is color AND ramp — comments and the bare-engine assertion say so

* fix(oklch): mix lands on each endpoint's hue bit-for-bit — unwrap the shorter arc by subtraction, then the same endpoint-exact lerp every axis uses

Hue took `(fromH + dh * t) % 360`, which at t = 1 is an addition of two
independently rounded values and reconstructs `toward.h` only by luck.
Now the larger endpoint of an arc wider than half a turn is taken a turn
down — `x - 360` for x ≥ 180 is exact by Sterbenz — and hue goes through
the same `lerp` as l/c/alpha; the final wrap adds 360 back to an exact
`x - 360`, whose real sum is representable, so it too is exact. Pinned
over a 6×6 grid of hue pairs at t = 0 and t = 1.

`wrapHue` is the one spelling of hue-into-[0, 360) and replaces the three
inline wraps in fromRgba, applyKey and mix.

docs(box): stop the getRowChars comment describing a reader that does not exist

The comment said `head*` holds the header content row's verticals "drawn by
the row renderer." No such wiring exists: _renderRow emits box.left and
box.vertical unconditionally, and after the separator fix nothing in src/
reads headLeft, headVertical, or headRight at all.

A caption naming a mechanism the code does not have is worse than no caption,
so the false clause is dropped rather than expanded. Wiring headVertical into
the header content row is rich-table-6uy.2, not this change.

fix(box): join the header to the body with the separator glyphs (rich-table-6uy.1)

A `Box` names its header CONTENT row verticals `head*` and its head-to-body
SEPARATOR glyphs `mid*`. `getRowChars` read "head" as "the head separator" and
reached for the verticals, so every table drew `┃━━━┃━━━┃` where the frame
wanted `┡━━━╇━━━┩` — wrong, but symmetric enough to read as plausible box art.

The glyph data was already right; only the field selection was wrong.

All four `RowLevel` arms now return the same tuple, because a `Box` carries one
separator set where Rich carries three (head_row, row, foot_row). That gap is
real and visible with `showLines`, where row separators draw the head-to-body
glyphs instead of `├───┼───┤`; it belongs to rich-table-6uy.3, which adds the
data. The arms are kept apart for it to fill.

The old tests pinned the defect and named the fields they expected, so they
could only ever pass by preserving it. Replaced with assertions on the rendered
separator. Reverting the fix turns all five red — checked, not assumed.

docs/tables.md's width ladder showed the old separator row; regenerated from
the renderer rather than redrawn by hand.
